description: Stable Phase 1 evaluation site portfolio. This set drives crawler implementation; the crawler is built against these sites, not the other way around.
rules: Sites MUST NOT be removed because the crawler struggles with them — struggling sites are the point of the portfolio.
A site may only be replaced when the site itself dies (career page permanently gone or company defunct); the replacement must cover the same category and the change must be recorded in `changelog`.
All URLs were verified live (HTTP 200 via GET) on lastVerifiedAt.
categories: ats-personio | ats-greenhouse | ats-lever | ats-workday | ats-recruitee | ats-smartrecruiters | ats-softgarden | ats-onlyfy | custom-html | custom-js | difficult
expectedAts values are best-effort expectations recorded before implementation; correcting them during Phase 1 is allowed and expected.

sites.name: Wemolo GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Canonical Personio-hosted board of a Munich scale-up; the most common ATS among German SMBs and a Tier 0 adapter target (Personio XML feed).
knownSpecialCharacteristics: JSON-LD JobPosting expected on job detail pages

sites.name: Vytal Global GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Second Personio tenant (Cologne) to prove the Personio adapter generalizes beyond one tenant.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: small posting volume — good for exact-count assertions

sites.name: everstox GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Third Personio tenant; company's own website blocks bots (HTTP 403), so the hosted board is the only crawlable surface — realistic constraint.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: company main site is bot-protected (403 to non-browser clients)

sites.name: happybrush GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Fourth Personio tenant, consumer brand; tenants occasionally churn on Personio (two candidates were already dead at selection time), so redundancy keeps the category alive.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: Personio tenant churn risk documented — keep as redundancy for the category

sites.name: GitLab Inc.
sites.reasonForInclusion: Canonical native Greenhouse board with high posting volume; Greenhouse has a public JSON API (boards-api.greenhouse.io) — Tier 0 adapter target.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: boards.greenhouse.io redirects to job-boards.greenhouse.io (URL scheme migrated — canonicalization test)
public Greenhouse boards JSON API available

sites.name: Celonis SE
sites.reasonForInclusion: Munich enterprise with a custom career site on top of Greenhouse — tests that the adapter finds the ATS behind a branded frontend instead of scraping the skin.

sites.name: N26 GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Berlin fintech with career pages inside the main marketing site; entry URL redirects by locale (en → en-eu) — discovery must survive locale redirects.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: career pages embedded in large marketing site — discovery noise

sites.name: Palantir Technologies
sites.reasonForInclusion: Canonical native Lever board; Lever has a public postings JSON API — Tier 0 adapter target.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: large volume, team/location filters via query params

sites.name: QuantCo, Inc.
sites.reasonForInclusion: Second Lever tenant with DACH presence; tenant slug ends in a hyphen ('quantco-') — a real-world edge case for URL/externalId derivation.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: tenant slug contains trailing hyphen — URL-parsing edge case

sites.name: NVIDIA Corporation
sites.reasonForInclusion: Canonical native Workday board; fully JS-rendered but backed by the well-known cxs JSON API — Tier 0 adapter target.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: no server-rendered job list — requires cxs API (…/wday/cxs/nvidia/…) or headless browser
very large posting volume, facet filters

sites.name: F. Hoffmann-La Roche AG
sites.expectedAts: Workday behind a Phenom CMS frontend (expected)
sites.reasonForInclusion: Swiss enterprise where the public career site is a separate CMS layer in front of the ATS — tests two-layer discovery (site → detail page → apply URL into Workday).
knownSpecialCharacteristics: frontend and ATS are different systems — applicationValue points into Workday
global site with country/language dimensions (CH anchor for the portfolio)

sites.name: everdrop GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Canonical Recruitee-hosted board (Munich consumer brand); Recruitee exposes a public offers JSON API — Tier 0 adapter target.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: JSON-LD JobPosting expected on detail pages

sites.name: rebuy recommerce GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Second Recruitee tenant (Berlin, mid-size) — proves the adapter generalizes; several first-choice Recruitee tenants were already dead at selection time, so redundancy matters here too.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: German-first postings, multiple Berlin locations per job

sites.name: BERNARD Gruppe ZT GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Austrian engineering group on Recruitee — AT anchor for the portfolio and a traditional (non-startup) employer profile.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: Austrian locations (Innsbruck, Wien) — AT country-code coverage

sites.name: Robert Bosch GmbH
sites.expectedAts: SmartRecruiters behind a custom search frontend
sites.reasonForInclusion: Huge German enterprise: custom search UI on jobs.bosch.com backed by SmartRecruiters (jobs.smartrecruiters.com/BoschGroup redirects here). Tests high-volume paginated search plus ATS-behind-frontend discovery.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: SmartRecruiters public posting API expected as Tier 0 path
many countries/languages — filtering to DACH needed

sites.name: Sixt SE
sites.reasonForInclusion: Canonical SmartRecruiters-hosted page of a Munich enterprise — the native-hosted counterpart to Bosch's custom frontend.

sites.name: MEDION AG
sites.reasonForInclusion: softgarden is a widespread German ATS not on the mandatory list — included deliberately so the portfolio contains an ATS without a planned Tier 0 adapter (forces the JSON-LD/recipe path).
knownSpecialCharacteristics: no Tier 0 adapter planned — must work via JSON-LD or recipe
DE/EN versions of the same postings

sites.name: NEW WORK SE (XING)
sites.reasonForInclusion: kununu's own corporate family on the onlyfy stack — strategically relevant ATS in the XING ecosystem, and a career section embedded in a corporate CMS site.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: onlyfy/Prescreen application flow expected on detail pages

sites.name: Zalando SE
sites.reasonForInclusion: Large Berlin tech employer with a fully custom, client-side career platform — the reference case for JS-heavy custom sites with no third-party ATS.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: internal JSON APIs behind the frontend

sites.name: Deutsche Bahn AG
sites.reasonForInclusion: One of Germany's largest employers; classic server-side search with page-number pagination and enormous volume — the reference pagination case.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: numbered pagination over tens of thousands of postings

sites.name: Lidl Dienstleistung GmbH & Co. KG
sites.expectedAts: custom frontend over an enterprise ATS (expected)
sites.reasonForInclusion: High-volume German retail employer; server-rendered listing pages with pagination and strong location structure — the retail counterpart to DB.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: store-level locations (thousands of near-duplicate postings differing only by city)

sites.name: dm-drogerie markt GmbH + Co. KG
sites.expectedAts: enterprise ATS behind custom frontend (expected SAP SuccessFactors)
sites.reasonForInclusion: Major German retailer whose entry domain redirects (.com → .de); SuccessFactors-style stack is common in German enterprises and is not on the Tier 0 list — must work via generic paths.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: no Tier 0 adapter planned for the expected ATS

sites.name: Spotify AB
sites.expectedAts: custom in-house career platform (migrated off Lever)
sites.reasonForInclusion: Fully custom SPA career site of a company that migrated off a supported ATS — represents the 'ATS assumptions rot over time' scenario.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: client-side rendered SPA, internal JSON API

sites.name: HelloFresh SE
sites.expectedAts: CMS career frontend over external ATS (expected; historically Greenhouse)
sites.reasonForInclusion: Berlin enterprise with a global career portal (auto-redirect to /global/en) layered over an ATS — a second two-layer case with different stack than Roche.

sites.name: Red Bull GmbH
sites.reasonForInclusion: Austrian flagship employer with a polished custom job platform; locale auto-redirect (→ /at-de) and load-more listing — the AT counterpart to Zalando.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: global brand — many non-DACH postings to filter

sites.name: CHECK24 Vergleichsportal GmbH
sites.expectedAts: custom, decentralized across many legal entities
sites.reasonForInclusion: Deliberately difficult: one brand, dozens of legal entities and city-specific subsidiaries posting separately — stresses externalId stability, dedup across near-identical postings, and discovery breadth.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: same role posted by multiple subsidiaries — near-duplicate handling

sites.name: MediaMarktSaturn Retail Group
sites.reasonForInclusion: Deliberately difficult: JS-heavy multi-brand, multi-country career portal with store-level postings — combines rendering, volume and locale problems in one site.

sites.name: DHL Group (Deutsche Post DHL)
sites.reasonForInclusion: Deliberately difficult: Avature-based global portal with geo-redirects (/ → /eu/de), heavy JS, session-bound search and known bot sensitivity — the portfolio's stress test. Not removable just because the crawler fails here.
knownSpecialCharacteristics: very large global volume, DACH filtering required
